subject: MAP: Capacity runway & staged GPU pool handoffs for Meditech pilot
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@meditech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Capacity runway & staged GPU pool handoffs for Meditech pilot

Hi Ariel / Tracy —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I’m attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out a phased capacity reservation approach for the pilot and production ramp. Key goals: keep your latency SLOs under 150ms p95 for interactive workflows, and limit committed spend in the early weeks while guaranteeing burst capacity during evals.

Highlights in the MAP (attached):
- Phase 0 (Eval): 2 x A100-80GB-equivalent slots for parallel evals, 2-week horizon.
- Phase 1 (Pilot): Staggered 4-slot GPU pool (mixed quantized LLMs) with prefix caching; expected start 6–8 weeks after signed commitment.
- Phase 2 (Prod ramp): 8–12 GPU pool target, autoscaling policies + fallbacks to smaller quantized variants.

We included a proposed handoff cadence: a 2-week technical on-ramp (SE-led), then a capacity reservation window (procurement commit), followed by a staged increase (tranche delivery). Procurement/lead time assumptions are called out in the MAP — generally 6–10 weeks from commit for Dedicated pools depending on region and SKU availability.

Please review the MAP and SOC2 evidence request I attached. I’d like to confirm:
1) A target go/no-go date for the pilot (we suggested 2026-04-15 in the spreadsheet).
2) Any hard constraints on committed GPU SKUs or vendor-preferred hardware (cloud marketplace vs. private on-prem).
3) Whether procurement wants a single commit or staged tranches across Q2/Q3.

I’m copying Marissa and Karthik for sizing and technical notes. Next step: 30-minute sync to finalize the MAP and sign-off timeline. I can do early next week.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

---

From: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@meditech.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tracy Huang <tracy.huang@meditech.com>, procurement@meditech.com
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Capacity runway & staged GPU pool handoffs for Meditech pilot

Thanks Sean — I reviewed the MAP and the phased approach looks sensible. A few items we need clarified before we present to procurement: 

- Can you provide a conservative lead-time estimate if we require Dedicated capacity in us-west with A100-80GB? Procurement is worried about a 10+ week lead time.
- For Phase 1 pilot sizing, can Marissa confirm we’ll maintain 150ms p95 when using the quantized variants you suggested?
- We may want to split the commitment: a small initial commit for pilot, then a tranche for Q3 based on usage. Will that be supported in contract language?

Also, a question on billing: is the initial eval billed at a reduced commit rate or fully consumption-based? Procurement will want that spelled out.

Appreciate it — Ariel

---

On Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@meditech.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Hi Ariel —

Short answers:
- Lead time: conservative estimate for Dedicated A100-80GB in us-west is 8–10 weeks from signed commitment if we need to provision reserved pool capacity (sometimes shorter if cloud-marketplace SKUs are available). We mark this per-region in the MAP to avoid surprises.
- Performance: For the pilot workload you described (128-token average, batched inference for 4 concurrent sessions), our internal tests show p95 ~120–140ms on quantized variants with continuous batching and prefix caching enabled. We’ll run a short pre-pilot eval with your test prompts to validate.
- Contract flexibility: We can structure a two-tranche commitment: a smaller Q2 pilot commit and a larger Q3 tranche with a mutually agreed ramp date. I’ll flag the legal points that need explicit tranche language (minimum notice, tranche activation lead time).

I attached a small technical appendix in the MAP workbook with assumptions and the validation checklist.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@meditech.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 13:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Capacity runway & staged GPU pool handoffs for Meditech pilot

Quick sizing note — based on the prompt mix you shared: 
- Eval (parallel): 2 x 80GB-equivalents is fine for 5–7 day stress tests. Use shorter max tokens to keep costs predictable.
- Pilot: Start with 4 mixed-precision slots (2 full FP16 / 2 4-bit quantized) to balance cost/latency while we collect traffic profile. This allows immediate fallbacks to fully quantized variants if burst demand spikes.
- Ramp: If daily QPS > 12 sustained for two weeks, move to 8-slot pool and enable autoscale headroom of 4 slots.

I’ll include a quick benchmark plan we can run in the pre-pilot window.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@meditech.com>

Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Capacity runway & staged GPU pool handoffs for Meditech pilot

This is helpful — thanks all. A couple of follow-ups from procurement: 
- Procurement prefers a staged commitment. They asked for wording that allows a pilot commit to convert into the larger tranche with 30 days’ notice, and a clearly defined tranche activation lead time.
- They want SOC2 evidence before signing; I see the PDF you attached. Can you also point them to the security contact for an evidence call?

Can we meet Wed 03 Mar at 09:30 PT for 30 minutes to finalize language?

Best,
Ariel

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@meditech.com>, procurement@meditech.com

Subject: Re: MAP: Capacity runway & staged GPU pool handoffs for Meditech pilot

Ariel / Procurement —

Confirmed for Wed 03 Mar time is tight so proposing Thu 04 Mar 09:30 PT instead. I’ve updated the MAP to include explicit tranche-activation language: pilot commit converts to tranche 2 with 30 days’ notice; tranche-activation lead time: 8 weeks (us-west Dedicated baseline) unless marketplace SKUs shorten that. I also added a clause for a limited conversion credit if tranche activation happens within 60 days.

Security contact for evidence call: Maya Srinivasan (security@redwood.com). She can run through the SOC2 artifacts and evidence scope.

Next actions:
- I’ll send the updated MAP workbook and a DocuSign for the pilot, marked as the first tranche.
- Marissa / Karthik will schedule a 2-hour pre-pilot validation window to run benchmarks with your prompts.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/drive/abc123-meditech-commit
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/421

If procurement is comfortable with the tranche wording, I’ll route the DocuSign tonight.

Thanks,
Sean

Attachments: Meditech_MAP_v1.xlsx (workbook, MAP + technical appendix); SOC2_evidence_request.pdf (security checklist)
